overview: Rise 5.99's Phase is a seven-mode movement exploit dispatched from onPreMotion with a different packet shape per mode. Normal nudges the server position by 0.005 through a silent C04 when collided horizontally and pushes a 1.5-block lateral C04 while inside a block; Forward teleports the local position by 0.5 with no packet at all; Vertical pairs a 0.5 lateral C04 with an 11-block up C04 carrying onGround false; Vanilla and Sand fly through blocks at the Fly Speed setting with the block-collide box nulled (Vanilla's enable sends a C04 with infinite coordinates before dropping 2 blocks); Clip snaps the player 3 blocks up or down once and disables; and Hypixel waits for a chat trigger, then relocates the player 4 blocks vertically or onto a target player via TPAura, but only after 10 grounded ticks with a solid block below. noClip is forced on every tick for every mode except Hypixel, and onDisable restores it.

sections.p: The module carries five settings (mode, Fly Speed, Hypixel Mode, Teleport Mode, Direction, Sneak Only) with onUpdateAlwaysInGui hiding them per mode, an onGroundTicks counter incremented in onPreMotion, and a canClip flag armed only by the Hypixel S02 chat listener. noClip is assigned from !mode.is("Hypixel") at the top of onPreMotion, so every non-Hypixel mode gets client-side noclip. The block-collide handler only nulls the collision box for Vanilla and Sand, and onMoveButton suppresses sneak for Vanilla, Sand and the sneak-gated modes so the noclip walk is not interrupted by a sneak-down. onEnable handles the one-shot modes: Clip teleports locally by plus or minus 3 per the Direction setting and immediately toggles the module off, and Vanilla sends the infinite-coordinate C04 then drops the local y by 2.

Normal computes x = sin(yaw) * 0.005 and z = cos(yaw) * 0.005; on horizontal collision it sends C04 at (posX - x, posY, posZ + z) with onGround true and mirrors the position locally, and while inside a block it sends a second C04 displaced 1.5 blocks along the yaw-perpendicular axis (cos(yaw + 90), sin(yaw + 90)) with onGround true, then strafes at half base speed. Forward uses the same 0.5 offsets but only calls setPosition, so the 0.5 displacement surfaces in the next regular C03 with no phase packet of its own. Vertical combines the two: the 0.5 lateral C04 (onGround true) plus an 11-block up C04 with onGround false, then the local setPosition. The 11-block move is the classic vertical-phase height: large enough to clear the block the client is stuck against, small enough to stay under the server's horizontal moved-too-quickly bound (which does not bound y at all).

Hypixel is the outlier: noClip stays off and the exploit is a timed ground relocation. canClip is armed when the S02 chat listener sees the player's own join message or the cage-open announcements; once armed, the PreMotion handler waits for onGround with onGroundTicks above 10 and a non-air block at (0, -0.9, 0), then in Auto mode setPosition is called with y moved by plus or minus (4 + random/500), in Teleport-Player mode TPAura.tpToLocation spams teleport packets with the 999/9.5/9.0 parameters toward the nearest eligible entity's position down 5 and the local position follows, and in Teleport-Middle mode the same spam targets the fixed BlockPos (0, 256, 0). canClip is cleared after one use, so each chat trigger permits exactly one relocation.

files.label: Phase.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is this 246-line file and nothing else. onPreMotion holds the mode switch with all packet sends (Normal's 0.005 and 1.5 lateral C04s, Vertical's lateral plus 11-block pair, Vanilla's infinite-coordinate C04, Hypixel's setPosition relocations) plus the noClip assignment; onBlockCollide nulls the box for Vanilla and Sand only; onPacketReceive is the Hypixel chat arming; onMoveButton clears sneak; onEnable runs the Clip and Vanilla one-shot sequences; onDisable restores noClip and the ground tick counter. Every C04 is sent through sendPacketWithoutEvent so the module's own packet event cannot re-intercept it.

files.label: PlayerUtil.java (block queries)
files.explanation: PlayerUtil supplies the block tests the modes depend on. isInsideBlock() is the overlap scan that gates the inside-block branches of Normal, Vertical, Vanilla and Sand; getBlockRelativeToPlayer(0, -0.9, 0) is the below-feet lookup the Hypixel mode uses to require a solid block under the player before relocating. Both are called from onPreMotion, so this file is the module's only external dependency beyond the movement utilities.

countering.label: Passable (swept-box ray trace)
countering.explanation: Passable ray-traces the swept collision volume between consecutive reported positions and flags transits whose box intersects a solid block's collision box, retrying alternate axis orders before accepting a clean move, and returns a set-back location on a hit with passableVL accumulation (1 per hit, 0.99 decay per clean move). The inside-block paths are direct hits: Normal's 1.5-block lateral C04 and Vanilla and Sand's fly-through moves are swept boxes crossing block faces, which the trace collides on. Normal's 0.005 nudge is sub-move and rides under the trace's resolution only when it does not cross a face; the moment the player is inside a block and the 1.5 C04 fires, the transit is flagged. Forward mode sends no phase packet, but its 0.5 local displacement appears in the next regular C03 as a from-to sweep through the wall, which the trace treats identically.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's vDistRel measures every vertical move against the momentum model: the allowance is seeded from the previous move's velocity and only named envelopes (zero-y ground moves, jumps, step-ups, riptide) are accepted. Vertical mode's 11-block C04 with onGround false is an 11-block rise against an allowance of a few tenths of a block, so yDistanceAboveLimit is around 10.7 and the violation (max(hdist,0) + max(ydist,0)) * 100 fires with a set-back; the onGround false flag cannot enter any envelope because it is not a jump. Vanilla's infinite-coordinate C04 presents an unbounded delta that violates on arrival regardless of the envelope. The 0.5 lateral C04s of Vertical and Forward are caught by the horizontal side: prepareSpeedEstimation predicts ~0.31 blocks per tick of sprint, so 0.5 gives hDistanceAboveLimit around 0.19 and a violation near 19 on the first move.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation: MorePackets scores every serverbound move packet into 500ms buckets against a 22/s window (20 ideal) with a half-second burst path (15 packets, 10 direct-violation). Vertical mode fires two extra C04s in the same tick as the regular move whenever the player is collided horizontally, and a sustained wall-hug under that mode triples the tick rate to about 60/s, blowing the window and tripping the burst path on the first concentrated burst. Normal's inside-block branch adds its lateral C04 the same way while the player is pinned in a wall. The check is content-blind, so the varied offsets and the onGround false on the 11-block move give no cover; the count is the tell.

countering.label: Phase (tesseract swept AABB)
countering.explanation: Hawk's Phase check inscribes the previous and current player boxes in a swept AABB, cuts it into a tesseract, and tests the volume against nearby solid blocks' collision boxes; a three-axis intersection punishes with rubber-band. Vanilla and Sand fly-throughs are textbook sweeps: the box travels through solid blocks at up to 9.5 blocks per tick (the Fly Speed maximum) and intersects every block along the path. Forward's packetless setPosition still produces a from-to sweep of 0.5 in the next C03, which the geometry catches the same way. The check's distance guard (distanceSquared > 65 returns early) is the honest gap: Vertical's 11-block C04 is 121 squared distance and is skipped, as is any pair spanning it, so the vertical envelope covers that branch. Normal's 0.005 nudge is inside the box-epsilon margins and typically passes; its 1.5 lateral C04 while inside a block does not.
